parts.text: Construct three candidate monospaced 18x20 bitmap fonts for the Gemini Supervisor reading-room cards. Historical inspiration should be High Middle Ages Germanic/Gothic scriptorium hands (early Gothic/Textura/book-hand traits), but machine-vision readability is the primary constraint. The cell geometry is fixed at exactly 18 pixels wide by 20 pixels high. Do not name existing fonts as the answer; construct usable pixel-font systems. Make candidate 1 the most OCR-safe, candidate 2 balanced, and candidate 3 the most strongly Gothic that still preserves reliable character separation. Return concrete machine-consumable JavaScript and representative exact 18x20 bitmaps. Ensure I/l/1, O/0, rn/m, c/e, braces/parentheses, quotes/backtick, slash/backslash, and Markdown/JSON/code punctuation remain visually distinct. Include a preview string that stresses those ambiguity pairs.

    {
      "name": "Scriptorium-OCR-Transitional",
      "historical_inspiration": "Early Protogothic / Carolingian-Textura transition (12th century), combining northern monastic ductus with humanist open counters.",
      "design_rules": [
        "Grid envelope: Baseline at row 15, x-height from row 7 to row 14 (8px), ascender line at row 2, descender line at row 18.",
        "Stem architecture: 2-pixel wide primary downstrokes; 45-degree single-pixel diagonal approach strokes.",
        "Disambiguation I/l/1: 'I' has symmetrical 6px serifs top and bottom; 'l' has a tall ascender with a 3px rightward rounded baseline hook; '1' features a 45-degree left downward flag (3px drop) and a closed bottom foot serif.",
        "Disambiguation O/0: 'O' is an upright oval counter without interior markers; '0' features a continuous 45-degree diagonal internal slash spanning row 6 to 14.",
        "Disambiguation rn/m: 'r' terminates with an angled rhomboid leaf at row 7 with right margin clearance; 'n' and 'm' enforce 2-pixel intra-stem whitespace and distinct right-foot baselines.",
        "Disambiguation c/e: 'e' features a rigid horizontal bar at row 10 and a closed upper counter; 'c' preserves an open 4-pixel right aperture.",
        "Punctuation & Brackets: Curly brace '{' has a distinct 2px center spine at row 10; '(' uses a smooth arc without center inflection; backtick '`' slants left-to-right (NW-SE) vs straight and right-to-left acute."
      ],
      "javascript": "function renderTransitional(char) { const grid = Array.from({length: 20}, () => Array(18).fill(0)); const drawRect = (x, y, w, h) => { for(let r = y; r < y + h; r++) for(let c = x; c < x + w; c++) if(r>=0&&r<20&&c>=0&&c<18) grid[r][c] = 1; }; const drawLine = (x1, y1, x2, y2) => { const dx = Math.abs(x2-x1), dy = Math.abs(y2-y1), sx = x1 < x2 ? 1 : -1, sy = y1 < y2 ? 1 : -1; let err = dx - dy, cx = x1, cy = y1; while(true) { if(cy>=0&&cy<20&&cx>=0&&cx<18) grid[cy][cx] = 1; if(cx===x2 && cy===y2) break; const e2 = 2*err; if(e2 > -dy) { err -= dy; cx += sx; } if(e2 < dx) { err += dx; cy += sy; } } }; switch(char) { case 'I': drawRect(6, 2, 6, 2); drawRect(8, 4, 2, 10); drawRect(6, 14, 6, 2); break; case 'l': drawRect(8, 1, 2, 13); drawRect(9, 14, 4, 2); drawRect(12, 12, 2, 2); break; case '1': drawLine(5, 5, 8, 2); drawRect(8, 2, 2, 12); drawRect(5, 14, 8, 2); break; case '0': drawRect(5, 4, 8, 12); for(let r=6; r<14; r++) for(let c=7; c<11; c++) grid[r][c]=0; for(let i=0; i<8; i++) grid[5+i][6+i]=1; break; case 'O': drawRect(5, 4, 8, 12); for(let r=6; r<14; r++) for(let c=7; c<11; c++) grid[r][c]=0; break; case 'r': drawRect(4, 7, 2, 8); drawRect(4, 7, 6, 2); drawRect(9, 8, 2, 2); break; case 'n': drawRect(4, 7, 2, 8); drawRect(6, 7, 5, 2); drawRect(11, 8, 2, 7); break; case 'm': drawRect(3, 7, 2, 8); drawRect(5, 7, 4, 2); drawRect(8, 8, 2, 7); drawRect(10, 7, 4, 2); drawRect(13, 8, 2, 7); break; case 'c': drawRect(5, 7, 8, 8); for(let r=9; r<13; r++) for(let c=7; c<13; c++) grid[r][c]=0; drawRect(12, 8, 1, 1); break; case 'e': drawRect(5, 7, 8, 8); for(let r=9; r<11; r++) for(let c=7; c<11; c++) grid[r][c]=0; for(let r=12; r<14; r++) for(let c=7; c<13; c++) grid[r][c]=0; drawRect(5, 10, 7, 2); break; } return grid.map(row => row.join('')); }",

    {
      "name": "Textura-SemiQuadrata-18",
      "historical_inspiration": "13th-14th century Gothic Textura Quadrata book hand, retaining distinct diamond-shaped finials (quadranguli) while enforcing strict OCR stem rhythm.",
      "design_rules": [
        "Stem width: 3 pixels solid downstroke with 45-degree corner quadrata terminals (3x3 rhomboid caps).",
        "Spacing rhythm: Fixed 3-pixel inter-stem gap across 'n', 'm', 'u', preventing the classical Textura 'picket-fence' collapse.",
        "Disambiguation rn vs m: 'r' uses a high, isolated quadrata node reaching rightward to column 12 with a severed lower drop; 'rn' contains an explicit 2-pixel gap between 'r' terminal and 'n' ascender, whereas 'm' has unbroken top shoulder arches.",
        "Disambiguation c vs e: 'e' incorporates a heavy horizontal bar at y=10 and a closed upper triangular loop; 'c' has an open right counter with a flared upper diamond serif.",
        "Braces and Delimiters: Braces '{' and '}' use sharp 90-degree fractured cusps at the middle height; parentheses '(' and ')' remain purely curved and slender.",
        "Quotes: Backtick '`' is built from a high diagonal descending left-to-right; straight quote '\"' uses two dual-column vertical bars with 2-pixel separation."
      ],
      "javascript": "function renderTextura(char) { const grid = Array.from({length: 20}, () => Array(18).fill(0)); const set = (x, y) => { if(x>=0&&x<18&&y>=0&&y<20) grid[y][x]=1; }; const stem = (x, y1, y2) => { for(let y=y1; y<=y2; y++) for(let w=0; w<3; w++) set(x+w, y); }; const diamond = (cx, cy) => { set(cx, cy-1); set(cx-1, cy); set(cx, cy); set(cx+1, cy); set(cx, cy+1); }; switch(char) { case 'I': stem(7, 4, 15); diamond(8, 3); diamond(8, 16); break; case '1': stem(8, 4, 16); set(7, 4); set(6, 5); set(5, 6); set(4, 7); for(let x=4; x<=13; x++) set(x, 16); break; case 'l': stem(7, 1, 15); diamond(7, 1); set(10, 15); set(11, 14); break; case '0': stem(4, 5, 14); stem(11, 5, 14); for(let x=5; x<=12; x++) { set(x, 4); set(x, 15); } set(8, 9); set(9, 10); break; case 'O': stem(4, 5, 14); stem(11, 5, 14); for(let x=5; x<=12; x++) { set(x, 4); set(x, 15); } break; case 'm': stem(2, 7, 15); stem(7, 7, 15); stem(12, 7, 15); for(let x=4; x<=7; x++) set(x, 7); for(let x=9; x<=12; x++) set(x, 7); break; case 'r': stem(4, 7, 15); for(let x=6; x<=11; x++) set(x, 7); set(11, 8); set(10, 9); break; case 'c': stem(4, 7, 14); for(let x=5; x<=11; x++) { set(x, 7); set(x, 14); } set(11, 8); break; case 'e': stem(4, 7, 14); for(let x=5; x<=11; x++) { set(x, 7); set(x, 10); set(x, 14); } set(11, 8); set(11, 9); break; } return grid.map(r => r.join('')); }",

      "name": "Fractur-Preservation-18",
      "historical_inspiration": "Late Medieval Fraktur / Bastarda scriptorium style, featuring broken curved strokes, double-lobed forms, and prominent angular ductus.",
      "design_rules": [
        "Broken stroke (Fraktur ductus): Verticals break inward at midpoint or inflection points.",
        "Zero distinction: '0' incorporates a bold central rectangular punctus (2x2 dot at row 9-10, col 8-9) with broken octagonal outer walls, contrasting with empty 'O'.",
        "Capital I vs digit 1 vs l: 'I' has double horizontal fractur bars and a central vertical twist; '1' has an exaggerated steep 60-degree diagonal left horn (width 5, height 6); 'l' uses a high vertical stem with a sharp 45-degree angled foot kicking up to row 12.",
        "Brackets vs Braces vs Slashes: Slashes '/' and '\\' span exactly from row 2 to 17 at strict 45-degree angle (14 pixels wide projection); Parentheses '(' maintain a wide 3-column curve; Braces '{' feature an acute broken cusp.",
        "Apertures: 'e' features a high diagonal stroke rising at 45 degrees, connecting to the upper crest, leaving a 2-pixel negative triangle; 'c' has an open mouth with an inward fang at row 8."
      ],
      "javascript": "function renderFractur(char) { const grid = Array.from({length: 20}, () => Array(18).fill(0)); const set = (x, y) => { if(x>=0&&x<18&&y>=0&&y<20) grid[y][x]=1; }; switch(char) { case '0': for(let y=4;y<=15;y++){ set(4,y); set(13,y); } for(let x=6;x<=11;x++){ set(x,3); set(x,16); } set(5,4); set(12,4); set(5,15); set(12,15); for(let y=9;y<=10;y++) for(let x=8;x<=9;x++) set(x,y); break; case 'O': for(let y=4;y<=15;y++){ set(4,y); set(13,y); } for(let x=6;x<=11;x++){ set(x,3); set(x,16); } set(5,4); set(12,4); set(5,15); set(12,15); break; case 'I': for(let x=4;x<=13;x++){ set(x,2); set(x,17); } for(let y=3;y<=9;y++) set(8,y); for(let y=10;y<=16;y++) set(9,y); set(7,9); set(10,10); break; case '1': for(let y=3;y<=16;y++) { set(9,y); set(10,y); } set(8,4); set(7,5); set(6,6); set(5,7); set(4,8); for(let x=5;x<=14;x++) set(x,16); break; case 'l': for(let y=1;y<=15;y++) { set(8,y); set(9,y); } set(10,14); set(11,13); set(12,12); break; case 'e': for(let y=7;y<=15;y++) set(4,y); for(let x=5;x<=12;x++){ set(x,7); set(x,11); set(x,15); } set(12,8); set(12,9); set(12,10); break; case '{': set(9,1); set(8,2); for(let y=3;y<=8;y++) set(7,y); set(6,9); set(5,10); set(6,11); for(let y=12;y<=17;y++) set(7,y); set(8,18); set(9,19); break; } return grid.map(r => r.join('')); }",
